milestones.name: An engine module can declare volume, cube and mipped-array textures in the frame, and wrong declarations are refused
milestones.bar: A frame graph that validates as Unreal's RDG and Unity's render graph do: a wrong declaration is refused when the graph is prepared, with a named error, and never becomes a wrong frame.

items.statement: A graph declares 3D, cube and mipped-array textures in transient, persistent and history scopes; on Metal a compute pass writes every texel of each kind and a later pass reads the same values back exactly, across a resize and a device replacement.
items.ask: Read the tests this check runs. Is every texel of each kind, every mip included, read back and compared exactly, and are the persistent and history cases rebuilt and compared again after device replacement?

items.statement: The compiler refuses each misuse the design lists: layers or multisampling on a 3D texture, a cube that is not six square layers, a storage write to a cube view, an attachment on a 3D texture, and a mip or layer range outside the descriptor. Transient reuse never crosses dimensions.
items.ask: Is there one refusal test for each misuse in the design's list, each asserting a named error, and a test that two transients that differ only in dimension never share an allocation?

items.statement: Against the capability record of the generation being compiled, the compiler refuses a storage format the record does not allow for that access, more storage textures in one pass than its limit, and an extent above its limit. The limits Chrome reports on this Mac are recorded.
items.ask: Does validation read only the capability record, with no device query in a pass? Does the evidence record the storage formats, storage-texture count and 3D extent that Chrome's record reports on this Mac?

items.statement: Every existing scene variant compiles to the same pass order, attachment storage and transient slots as before this milestone.
items.ask: Which test pins the compiled pass names, order and attachment storage of the day, night and capture variants, and did any of them change in this milestone's diff?

items.statement: APPLE-TILE's M0 exact matrix passes on a release build of the claimed commit: this milestone moved no retained Mac image. Chrome's baseline is not checked here; the design says when it is.
items.check: cargo build --locked --offline --release -p v1-game --features draw-probe,thrum-render/creation-counters && cargo build --locked --offline --release -p thrum-cook && rm -rf tmp/exact-m0 && mkdir -p tmp/exact-m0 && target/release/thrum-cook cook examples/v1-game/assets/showcase tmp/exact-m0/valley && python3 scripts/apple_tile_m1.py --store tmp/exact-m0/valley --output tmp/exact-m0/m1 && python3 scripts/apple_tile_m2.py --store tmp/exact-m0/valley --output tmp/exact-m0/m2

milestones.name: A test effect keeps its simulation in step with the world through dropped frames, pauses and a replaced device, on Mac and in Chrome
milestones.bar: State that behaves like the persistent simulations of a shipped game, such as Sea of Thieves' sea: it moves with the world's clock, never with the frame rate. A repeated tick or a pause changes nothing, and a hitch, a dropped frame or a device loss leaves no jump, smear or stale texel.

items.statement: A scene holds several contributions in a fixed order: the cooked valley and the diagnostic effect draw together, and with no effect attached every existing scene compiles to the same passes as before.
items.ask: Does the public seam let a crate outside thrum-render declare resources and passes with no access to renderer internals, and does the cooked contribution compile and draw unchanged?

items.statement: After a scripted run that mixes submitted frames, several frames in one tick, a pause, a discarded frame, a capture frame, a stall of many ticks, a backward tick, a timeline change and a resize, the effect's GPU state matches the design's state table bit for bit: a nonempty field is unchanged by the repeated ticks and the pause, and is at its declared reset after the backward tick and after the timeline change. Its wrapping anchor equals the last committed one.
items.ask: Read the scripted run. Are the kept-state and reset expectations written from the design's state table, not taken from stepping code the GPU path shares? Is the field nonempty before the repeated ticks and the pause? Are the ticks a stall dropped beyond the declared bound counted?

items.statement: A pass's cadence changes at run time with no graph compilation and no pipeline creation. With two ping-pong histories updated at different cadences, a consumer reads each history's newest submitted result on every frame: the tentative side when its producer ran, the committed side when it was skipped, and the committed side again after a frame whose update was discarded. The first frame of an epoch and a reset frame write every texel.
items.ask: Does the test read back the consumer's own output on each run-to-skip and skip-to-run boundary of both histories and after the discarded update, and every texel after the first frame of an epoch and after a reset? Does the compiler refuse each declaration the design's cadence section lists?

items.statement: After device replacement the effect rebuilds on the new generation, re-seeds through its declared reset, uses no resource of the old generation and matches the CPU oracle again.

In Chrome the same scripted run ends with the effect's state matching the same expectations, through a device loss and recovery, with the cube, every texel of the volume and every mip of the array read back exactly.

In real time on the Mac the diagnostic trail persists and fades after its source stops, stays fixed to the ground as the camera pans across the wrapping boundary, and shows no jump when the cadence changes.
items.inspect: Capture with T2 engine capture in `realtime` mode: the source moving and then stopping, a pan that carries the anchor across at least one wrap, and a cadence change mid-run. Judge the trail in whole frames and native-size crops as consecutive frames at 1x.

items.statement: With no effect attached, the frame records show no added pass, resource or copy; with the diagnostic attached, per-pass GPU time, read from the executor's named pass timings, and bytes per effect are recorded on the valley route.
items.ask: Do the frame records with no effect attached list exactly the passes they listed before this milestone? Are the diagnostic's per-pass times and resource bytes recorded with the load, from the executor's named pass timings and without changing the host's frame-sample fields, which APPLE-TILE M3 owns?

items.statement: Every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes the verifier at the claimed commit: this milestone moved no retained image.

milestones.name: A test effect draws through the scene as water or cloud would, hidden by nearer objects, and hands its motion to reconstruction, on Mac and in Chrome
milestones.bar: A translucent pass that composes as water does in Sea of Thieves or glass in a shipped engine: hidden by nearer geometry in the same frame, refracting what is behind it, dimming sky and stars once, with no seam where it meets opaque surfaces. Its motion, reactive coverage and reset reach reconstruction's inputs exactly. How a reconstructed effect looks in motion is judged in SEA and CLOUDS, not here.

items.statement: An after-opaque pass draws after opaque geometry, sky and stars and before the pre-tone input, and reads this frame's scene depth. Stored depth and the colour copy follow separate requests: a depth-only effect stores depth and adds no copy pass, a refracting effect adds one shared copy, and with no effect nothing is added beyond what other readers, such as reconstruction, already store.
items.ask: Does a moving occluder hide the slab in the same frame, proving it reads this frame's depth? Do the compiled graphs for the four cases (no effect with reconstruction off, no effect with reconstruction on, a depth-only effect, a refracting effect) each hold exactly the storage and passes their declared accesses require?

items.statement: The slab's pixels carry motion from unjittered positions and reactive coverage in submitted frames, mark history invalid where it has none, and honour the frame's reset flag on a cut, a device replacement and an effect reset. This proves reconstruction's inputs; reconstructed output is not judged here.
items.ask: Are the motion and reactive values read from submitted frames and compared with the slab's known displacement, with temporal sampling selected?

items.statement: A simulate pass declared async-eligible is checked (compute only, no attachment or surface access) and listed in the compiled graph; the pass order is the same with and without the flag.

Each cadence is a listed quality knob with a range and a declared invalidation; a change commits at a frame boundary and applies that invalidation, and a skipped pass is reported as not run under its own pass name.
items.ask: Can a caller that knows nothing about the effect list its knobs and set one, as the governor will? Does the timing record tell a skipped pass from a pass that took no time?

items.statement: In Chrome the slab draws after opaque geometry with the same depth, refraction and motion behaviour, and is cut cleanly by nearer geometry.
items.inspect: Capture a `fixed` still in Chrome with T2 engine capture, with the slab crossing terrain, a prop and open sky. Judge the whole frame and a native-size crop of each crossing.

items.statement: On both native recipes the slab is cut cleanly by nearer geometry, refracts the scene behind it, dims the sky and stars behind it once, and leaves no seam where it meets opaque surfaces.
items.inspect: Capture `fixed` stills with T2 engine capture at noon and at night, on the portable and Apple tile recipes, with the slab crossing terrain, a prop and open sky. Judge whole frames and native-size crops of each crossing.

items.statement: The seam is documented for the modules that will use it, the cost of the refraction copy and the pass break is recorded on both native recipes, and the maturity ledger has a row for the seam.
items.ask: Could the SEA or CLOUDS planner write their passes from the public documentation and this design alone? Are the copy and pass-break costs recorded as paired rows with the load, and does the ledger keep implementation, correctness and device results apart?

items.statement: Every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes the verifier at the claimed commit: this milestone moved no retained image.
